note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: On an attached perennial shoot find relatively broad lanceolate stem blades, commonly 7–15 mm wide in the WFO regional treatment (Go Botany lists 5–10 mm), sometimes cordate/clasping at the base. Follow the same culm to an open, relatively few-spikeleted spring panicle (about 5–10 cm in the WFO treatment). The eight stored source-identified photos show live leafy shoots, open panicles and flowering spikelets, but do NOT establish a rooted voucher, exact blade-base shape, true inner ligule or species by themselves.
tiles.short: Broad, often heart-based stem leaves + small open panicle; confirm the collar and spikelet
tiles.status: FIELD-READY COMBINED CUE — SOURCE-IDENTIFIED, NOT MEASURED SAME-PLANT PROOF

tiles.heading: 02 · FOLLOW THE GROWTH FORM
tiles.details: Trace an entire attached shoot and record its root crown, spring primary flowering panicle and later-season leafy secondary branches if available. The source describes a perennial with branching stems, and many Dichanthelium have seasonally different flowering phases. Do not assert that a dense winter rosette is always visible in D. commutatum: treatments differ on basal-rosette expression. Current woodland-habit photo shows shoots meeting litter, NOT an exposed connected perennial crown.
tiles.short: Perennial branching grass; spring and late-season shoots can differ
tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — CONNECTED CROWN AND SEASONAL SHOOTS

tiles.heading: 03 · OPEN THE TRUE COLLAR
tiles.details: Peel the blade away from its sheath and inspect the INNER blade–sheath junction under 10–20× with a millimeter scale. The USGS Louisiana key gives a ~0.5-mm ligule; Go Botany gives up to 0.5 mm; WFO notes a minute hair fringe or absence, depending on treatment. Distinguish the actual ligule from long marginal/sheath hairs. Existing Alex Abair collar images show OUTER hairs and leaf junction only, not a measured free inner ligule.
tiles.short: True ligule minute, often about 0–0.5 mm; do not measure sheath-edge hairs
tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — TRUE INNER LIGULE AT 0.1–1 MM SCALE

tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE MATURE SPIKELETS
tiles.details: Measure at least three mature, source-vouchered oval spikelets from the SAME rooted flowering plant against a 1-mm scale at 10–20×. WFO gives ~2.1–3.2 mm; Go Botany ~2.2–3.2 mm. Panicle macro panels show real oval spikelets and fine pedicels, but their images have no calibration. Flower colors, hairiness and panicle openness cannot substitute for mature measurements.
tiles.short: Typically ~2.1–3.2 mm long; photograph three with a real scale

tiles.heading: 05 · SEPARATE GLUMES AND LEMMAS
tiles.details: Under a dissecting lens separate the FIRST/LOWER glume (WFO usually about one-third or a little more of the 2.1–3.2-mm spikelet; Nicaragua treatment ~0.5–1.5 mm), upper glume, lower sterile-floret lemma and firm upper fertile lemma/palea. The fertile lemma has NO awn (Go Botany: 0 mm), so never label a visible flower filament, purple anther or red stigma as an awn. A partly opened existing source photograph exposes pale surfaces, but individual glume/lemma boundaries and veins have NOT been independently resolved or measured.
tiles.short: Short lower glume; upper glume + lower sterile lemma; upper fertile lemma awnless
tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — DISSECTED GLUMES, FERTILE LEMMA AND SCALE; NO ORGAN ARROWS YET

tiles.heading: 06 · SEPARATE LOCAL LOOK-ALIKES
tiles.details: D. lindheimeri usually has much smaller ripe spikelets (~1.3–1.6 mm) and a conspicuous longer collar hair fringe. D. oligosanthes overlaps in broad foliage but usually has larger spikelets (~2.9–4 mm) and a longer hair fringe. D. pedicellatum has narrower spring blades (~1.3–5.5 mm) and a very short ~0.25–0.5-mm fringe; its ~3–3.5-mm spikelets overlap D. oligosanthes. These are literature comparisons, not calibrated in current look-alike panels. Record Dichanthelium sp. when the same-plant leaf base, true collar and mature spikelets cannot be reconciled.
tiles.short: Leaf base + true ligule + measured spikelets beat airy-head guesses
tiles.status: FIELD-READY LOOK-ALIKE KEY — SPECIES CONFIRMATION STILL REQUIRES CALIBRATED EVIDENCE

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: VARIABLE PANICGRASS: first find the broad, often somewhat heart-based stem leaves and true short or absent hair ligule on a rooted shoot. Existing reproductive photo is GREAT for SEEING anthers, feathery red stigmas and a hairy spikelet, but cannot prove the leaf base, size, or species. Confirm a mature 2.1–3.2 mm spikelet and leaf-base/collar before calling D. commutatum.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: 1. Confirm original photo ROLE (flower macro, habitat view, or open panicle) before using a label; this image alone is NOT a verified same-plant key.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Peel the blade away from its sheath and inspect the INNER blade–sheath junction under 10–20× with a millimeter scale. The USGS Louisiana key gives a ~0.5-mm ligule; Go Botany gives up to 0.5 mm; WFO notes a minute hair fringe or absence, depending on treatment. Distinguish the actual ligule from long marginal/sheath hairs. Existing Alex Abair collar images show OUTER hairs and leaf junction only, not a measured free inner ligule.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Measure at least three mature, source-vouchered oval spikelets from the SAME rooted flowering plant against a 1-mm scale at 10–20×. WFO gives ~2.1–3.2 mm; Go Botany ~2.2–3.2 mm. Panicle macro panels show real oval spikelets and fine pedicels, but their images have no calibration. Flower colors, hairiness and panicle openness cannot substitute for mature measurements.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Against tiny-spikeleted D. lindheimeri (~1.3–1.6 mm) check actual size and hair ligule; against D. oligosanthes (~2.9–4 mm) compare broad sometimes cordate stem leaf base and very short/absent true ligule; against D. pedicellatum (~3–3.5 mm) compare broader stem leaves vs narrow blades and extremely short 0.25–0.5 mm collar fringe. All photos source-determined, not Hays vouchers.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: Variable panicgrass — live woodland habit with leafy flowering shoots
panels.caption: Alex Abair's exact-species field image shows upright branching grassy shoots, attached broad stem blades, terminal airy flowering panicles and an understory floor of leaf litter. Multiple plants overlap, so do not claim every nearby blade belongs to one rooted plant. Roots, tillering crown, true inner ligule and connected belowground structures are not visible.

panels.caption: Alex Abair's actual macro resolves conspicuous hairs lining the sheath and leaf-attachment margins on an intact flowering culm. The narrow stem continues above the junction. This is NOT a calibrated 0.5-mm TRUE INNER ligule image: do not confuse outer sheath-margin hair tufts or cobweb filaments with the inner ligule.

panels.label: Variable panicgrass — broad attached stem blade
panels.caption: This photographed leaf has a relatively broad lanceolate blade, acute tapering tip, and its base visibly attaching to the stem at the upper right. Fine parallel venation and subtle blade-edge texture are visible. DO NOT diagnose a measurable clasping/heart-shaped base or a 0.5-mm inner ligule from these exterior pixels alone.

panels.label: TRUE LEAF BASE — clasping blade and purple sheath mouth
panels.caption: Alex Abair's photo shows a green blade emerging to the right from the purplish stem sheath, with the blade base curving round the culm and wispy hairs near the junction. The real sheath continues down the culm to a dark swollen-looking node lower in the photograph. The interior ligule edge is NOT exposed or scaled, so do not mistake the sheath overlap for a measured 0.5-mm ligule.

panels.label: FIELD LESSON — leafy branching shoots and tight leaf clusters
panels.caption: This older rockerBOO species-labelled photograph shows narrow green blades on low branching culms and conspicuous groups of short leaves at shoot junctions amid woodland debris. The photograph does not prove an excavated rooted crown, exact seasonal phenology, inner ligule or measured spikelets.

intro: VARIABLE PANICGRASS: first find the broad, often somewhat heart-based stem leaves and true short or absent hair ligule on a rooted shoot. Existing reproductive photo is GREAT for SEEING anthers, feathery red stigmas and a hairy spikelet, but cannot prove the leaf base, size, or species. Confirm a mature 2.1–3.2 mm spikelet and leaf-base/collar before calling D. commutatum.
memory_rule: ROSETTE + LEAF BASE + TRUE COLLAR → THREE MEASURED SPIKELETS. 1.3–1.6 LIN; 2.1–3.2 COM; 2.9–4 OLI; 3–3.5 PED (mm; OLI/PED overlap).
safety_note: The literature-size figures and diagnostic leaf features are not verified by the stored photos. Do not attach falsely precise or microscopic arrows.
field_rule: Panicles often overlap. Show spring/autumn phase, true leaf collar, and at least three mature measured spikelets from the same plant before a firm species call.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
